name: Mugamoodi
summary: Tamil cinema's masked kung fu hero from Mysskin's 2012 film, a Chennai graduate who becomes a superhero to win a policeman's daughter and fights a gang boss.
origin: Anand is a kung fu-trained college graduate in Chennai, nicknamed Bruce Lee. To impress Shakthi, the daughter of a police officer, he takes on a masked hero persona on his grandfather's advice. He is later framed for his friend's murder and faces Dragon, a gang boss linked to his own martial arts teacher.
powers: Kung fu fighting trained in Wing Chun-style martial arts
Masked costume with gadgets designed with IIT consultants
Stunt work at great heights, including a port climax

storyline.title: A kung fu school in Chennai
storyline.beat: Anand, nicknamed Bruce Lee, trains in martial arts with out-of-work friends and tries to recruit students to save their school. Along the way he falls for Shakthi, a police officer's daughter.

storyline.title: A borrowed costume
storyline.beat: On his grandfather's advice Lee borrows a superhero costume and introduces himself to Shakthi as Mugamoodi. He wows children, helps the police catch a bandit and becomes the city's talk.

storyline.title: A friend lost
storyline.beat: A gang member shoots Shakthi's father and the family blames Lee. When his friend Viji is killed and Lee is found beside him, the police chase him, so his grandfather and brother sew him a brand-new suit.

storyline.title: The hospital fight
storyline.beat: The gang attacks the hospital to finish off the officer's family. Lee defeats them as Mugamoodi and takes the case file, which leads him to his own kung fu teacher and to the gang boss Dragon.

storyline.title: Showdown at the port
storyline.beat: The gang takes over a port with 30 children and three adults as hostages. Lee faces Dragon, is unmasked, then fights through with help from his grandfather and friends, and Shakthi urges him to keep being Mugamoodi.

gossip.text: Suriya was once reported as the lead of this film, opted out in 2009 over dates, and later helped unveil the first look in June 2012.
Reports of Akkineni Nageswara Rao joining the cast proved false, and Girish Karnad played the grandfather.
Pooja Hegde made her film debut in Mugamoodi, after finishing as second runner-up at Miss Universe India 2011.
Film Companion says the crowd before the first-day first show felt like a heavy-metal concert, with fans who grew up on Bruce Lee and Jackie Chan video cassettes.

quiz.why: The hero is Anand, a kung fu graduate nicknamed Bruce Lee.

quiz.q: Which martial arts legend is Mugamoodi dedicated to?
quiz.why: Mysskin dedicated the film to Bruce Lee, which is also why the hero is nicknamed Bruce Lee.

quiz.q: Which actor made her film debut in Mugamoodi?
quiz.why: Pooja Hegde debuted as Shakthi, the police officer's daughter.

quiz.q: What did the Telugu version of Mugamoodi get titled?
quiz.why: The Telugu dub was titled Mask.

quiz.q: About how many different masks were made for Mugamoodi before one was chosen?
quiz.why: Behindwoods reports a dozen suits and over 30 masks were made.

theme.tagline: A mask, a kung fu school and a Chennai sky.

timeline.title: First look and trailer
timeline.note: On 29 June 2012 Suriya and Gautham Menon unveil the first look, and the trailer launches at Sathyam Cinemas in Chennai.

timeline.title: Soundtrack launch
timeline.note: The album is launched on 1 August 2012 at Sathyam Cinemas, presented by Vijay and received by Puneeth Rajkumar.

timeline.title: Release across languages
timeline.note: The film opens on 31 August on over 600 screens, dubbed as Mask in Telugu and Mahabali Ek Super Hero in Hindi.

timeline.title: Ten crore weekend
timeline.note: Despite mixed reviews, the film earns about Rs 10 crore over its first three days.

timeline.title: Sequel talk
timeline.note: Reports say Mysskin has a Mugamoodi 2 script, possibly in 3D, while Jiiva asks for a lighter costume before returning.

timeline.title: Debut nominations
timeline.note: Pooja Hegde is nominated for Best Female Debut at the Filmfare South awards on 20 July 2013, one of several nominations for the film.

timeline.title: Asian superhero list
timeline.note: A Yahoo roundup of top 10 Asian superhero movies includes it and calls it the first Tamil superhero movie.

facts.text: Mysskin dedicated Mugamoodi to Bruce Lee, and the hero is a kung fu-trained Chennai graduate nicknamed Bruce Lee before he ever puts on the mask.

Hong Kong-based costume designer Gabriella Wilkins, whose earlier work included Disneyland and Cirque du Soleil, led ten assistants for six months and made a dozen suits and over 30 masks before Mysskin picked one.
Jiiva sat through an eight-hour head-casting session in Hong Kong so the mask could fit his face precisely.

Producers said stunt coordinator Tony Leung Siu-hung had worked on Bruce Lee's Enter the Dragon. He taught the lead cast Wing Chun and designed five of the film's action sequences, according to Behindwoods.
The big stunt scenes were filmed at Karaikal port, where the lead actor performed daredevil stunts about 180 feet up, over the port's conveyor belt.
Jiiva said the costume was so heavy that eating, sitting or standing was a struggle, and it left him with a neck problem. He shot for about 80 nights, mostly after dark.
The hero has three names: Anand, which his father calls him, Bruce Lee, which he calls himself, and Mugamoodi. Film Companion counts three superhero costumes across the film, too.
The hero's face stays hidden until someone shouts the name Bruce Lee, and the opening shot is a blue wall that melts into the blue of his shirt.
Lee first puts on a makeshift costume to meet Shakthi because she thinks he is a street ruffian, so the mask begins as a way to win her over.
Jiiva said Mugamoodi is not a superhero in the real sense: he has no super powers and uses only his mind and body, like one of the public.
Jiiva began kung fu at about 16 only to avoid early-morning jogging with his father, then trained 1998 to 2002, and his teacher also had him learn gymnastics.
Jiiva was not a superhero comic reader. He said he grew up more a fan of Rambo and Commando, though he enjoyed Superman, Batman and Spider-Man films.
Wing Chun is a close-combat style that the cast learned for the film. Jiiva said that if there is a sequel he wants to train for weeks at a time with Tony Leung to fight like a professional.
Mugamoodi was claimed to be the first superhero film in Tamil cinema, and a 2015 Yahoo list of top Asian superhero movies describes it the same way.
The high-tech gadgets were reportedly designed by IIT consultants and costume teams came from NIFT. The crew visited four countries to finalise Jiiva's suit, settling in Hong Kong.
Jiiva and Narain trained in kung fu for three months, and a young group of fighters spent over six months learning at a kung fu school in Nandanam, Chennai, to fill the action scenes.
Before Jiiva, the lead was linked to Suriya in 2008, Vishal in 2009 and Arya in 2010. Suriya reportedly planned to learn martial arts, and the film was first reported at a huge ₹35 crore budget.
Mysskin said he wanted the superhero to do only what a real person could, so that Indian audiences would accept it and not laugh at it.
The climax at Karaikal port was planned as a 20-day shoot, and Hong Kong stunt coordinator Tony Leung Siu Hung joined it in May 2012.
Jiiva's father, producer R. B. Choudary, acquired the Telugu rights and that version was called Mask. The Hindi dub was titled Mahabali Ek Super Hero, released across over 600 screens.

kidSummary: Mugamoodi is Tamil cinema's masked kung fu hero. Anand, nicknamed Bruce Lee, borrows a superhero suit to impress a girl and ends up facing a gang boss named Dragon at a port.
